description: Participants build and evaluate applications that see, listen and speak, with Arabic as the main case. For the fictional Heritage Trails Authority they extract grounded fields from visitor and ranger photos with vision-language models, benchmark open-weight speech recognisers on dialects and code-switched speech, test synthesised read-back, and assemble a bilingual voice booking line with turn-taking, interruption and tool calls within a latency budget. They test it with simulated callers and choose between open-weight and hosted, cascaded and speech-to-speech designs on measured quality, latency and cost. Photos are public-domain or synthetic; calls use synthetic voices and public speech corpora.
audience: Specialists. Engineers who have completed the level 300 core and the practicum, or can show equivalent work: an AI system they built, operated and defended in review.
prerequisites: AE-301 Applied Natural Language Processing Engineering
AE-303 Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications
Has built a language model application with structured outputs and tool calls
Computes precision, recall and an error rate with an interval

outcomes.text: Implement image applications with vision-language models that return validated structured fields grounded in the image, given 60 visitor and ranger photos with reference fields and boxes
outcomes.evidence: an extraction pipeline with field accuracy and grounding scores on the test set

outcomes.text: Evaluate speech recognisers on Arabic dialects and code-switched speech with explicit normalisation rules, given two open-weight recognisers and a sliced set of public and synthetic clips
outcomes.evidence: an error-rate report by dialect and channel with intervals and the normalisation rules used

outcomes.text: Build a bilingual voice agent that handles turn-taking, interruption and confirmed tool calls within a latency budget, given a booking tool and a budget for time to first audio
outcomes.evidence: a running agent with per-stage latency traces from twenty scripted calls

outcomes.text: Diagnose failure modes specific to image and audio inputs, including invented objects, text produced on silence and instructions hidden in images, given seeded failing inputs for each modality
outcomes.evidence: a failure log with causes and a mitigation tested for each mode

outcomes.text: Design a multimodal test set and an end-to-end evaluation with simulated callers, given the full booking and reporting system
outcomes.evidence: a test set with a coverage table across modality, dialect and task, and graded results

outcomes.text: Decide between open-weight and hosted, cascaded and speech-to-speech designs on quality, latency and cost per call, given measured results for two pipelines
outcomes.evidence: a one-page decision record with the measurements and a script that a reviewer re-runs to the same figures
